newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Minister seeks lower Russia fuel, transport prices.
newsitem.headline: Minister seeks lower Russia fuel, transport prices.

text.p: Russia needs lower prices for energy, transport and communications to stimulate economic growth, newly appointed First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said in a television interview.
"We need to lower prices," Nemtsov, appointed last week, told NTV commercial television on Sunday night. "Work with the natural monopolies is the basis for the regeneration of the whole economy."

He said lower prices would be achieved by restructuring and through government regulation, but he ruled out breaking up the monopolies into regional units and did not make clear exactly what the government intended to do.

"I can say immediately that no matter what models of demonopolisation are presented later on, (energy giant) United Energy Systems (UES) will stay and the existing single system of gas supply will stay," Nemtsov said.

Nemtsov, who has said he is ready to make unpopular decisions to force through reforms, said some restructuring could bring an element of competition, such as allowing electricity producers to sell directly to consumers instead of to UES, the current middleman.
"What we're talking about is allowing energy producers, using UES, to compete among themselves. The consumer will then buy from whoever is cheapest and works the best," he said.
Nemtsov singled out gas firm Gazprom as a positive example of a natural monopoly. The company's prices were already low compared to world prices and internal reforms were under way.
"(Gazprom) is the least harmful of the natural monopolies," he said, calling it Russia's national treasure.
"The involvement of the government here has to lead towards increasing the value of the company and increasing the price of its shares so as to attract investment."
Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev said on Monday that the company was ready to meet Nemtsov to discuss the proposals as well as the company's own internal reforms.
"We are ready any time to talk about what we are doing and why we are doing it," Itar-Tass news agency quoted him as saying.
"It would be good if the programme that we are carrying out coincided with government opinion. If it doesn't, we will have to continue the dialogue."
